diet.text: Mainly toads; also frogs, lizards, insects

overview.text: Wagler's Snake is a toad-eating, rear-fanged snake of eastern South America.

identification.text: Very variable: some are plain reddish-tan, others pale brown with broad black-edged dark crossbands.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Venezuela, the Guianas, Brazil, Bolivia, Paraguay, Uruguay and northern Argentina.

habitat.text: Open savanna and shrubland up to 2,000 m, and disturbed places.

diet.text: Insects, frogs, toads, lizards and sometimes snakes. Its enlarged back teeth puncture toads that puff themselves up, making them easier to swallow.

funfacts.text: Toads puff themselves up to be hard to swallow - this snake's long back teeth let the air out!
